chapter: Heroes, heard bands and Lunceford's life on the road
title: Replacing Walter Conyers in the Army Service Force band
summary: Crawford recalls Walter Conyers, the band's earlier drummer, and the unit led by Clarence Rawls with Joe Turner, Sy Oliver and Bob Carroll.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: When I went in the Army, boy standing right here in this living room by the name of Walter [Kindness.] He said; you know, when you came in the Army -- he was talking in front of his wife -- you came in to serve for me, and then you got in the band, and you played -- you just played hard. He said, that was the thing that kept me out of the band and, you know, like to go -- well, there was another drummer in there also by the name of Buster, little West Indian boy. Now, he had some nice, fast hands. He could do his single strokes very good.
Walter more or less wanted to be a flash drummer.

He didn't have it in himself. Well, that's -- he died here some time ago, and that hurt me more than a lot of things that I know. His wife was here. You know, she didn't let us know that he died for some reason. We got it from some other source, Jerry Wayne, I think, to relate his name, a friend of [Saint Cicao], who -- she told us that Walter Conyers has died, passed.
But he's a guy you met in the service, and you replaced him in the band.
Yes, he was a drummer in the band.
You took the job from him?

They called me there -- see, they didn't let -- call too many musicians. What I mean, that particular outfit was led by Clarence [Rawls] who was a sergeant in the Army, and called guys like Joe Turner on piano. Naturally, he wanted Sy Oliver over there. And Bob Carroll, used to hang out there at the Rhythm Club. And -- who was unbelievably -- just a cruel, big rascal. He and Ben Webster, I was told, I heard about it, got in the darndest fight. And Ben Webster liked that. He blackened everything he could find on Bob Carroll.
